Digital 9 Infrastructure PLC

DIGITAL 9 INFRASTRUCTURE PLC
("D9" or the "Company")
CHANGE OF AUDITOR
Digital 9 Infrastructure plc announces that, following a competitive tender process, it has appointed Johnston Carmichael LLP ("Johnston Carmichael") as the Company's external auditor for the financial year ending 31 December 2026.
Johnston Carmichael has been granted Recognised Auditor status by the Jersey Financial Services Commission. The appointment will be subject to shareholder approval at the Company's 2027 Annual General Meeting.
PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP ("PwC") has served as the Company's external auditor since March 2021 and ceased to hold office with effect from 3 September 2026. As the Company is incorporated in Jersey, PwC's cessation has been conducted in accordance with the Companies (Jersey) Law 1991 rather than the Companies Act 2006. In accordance with Article 113B(9) of that Law, PwC has confirmed to the Company that there are no circumstances connected with its ceasing to hold office which it considers should be brought to the notice of the Company's members or creditors.
END

latest.content:

Digital 9 Infrastructure PLC

DIGITAL 9 INFRASTRUCTURE PLC
("D9" or the "Company")
Interim Results
for the six-month period ended 30 June 2026
The Board of Digital 9 Infrastructure plc announces the Company's unaudited Interim Results for the six-month period ended 30 June 2026.
The Interim Report has been published and is available to view on the Company's website at:
https://www.d9infrastructure.com/investors/
.
Shareholders wishing to discuss the Interim Results are welcome to request a meeting with representatives of the Investment Manager by emailing
D9@ircp.com
.
Eric Sanderson, Chair of D9, said:
"This has been a milestone period for D9. We returned £30 million to shareholders through our first compulsory redemption since the wind-down began, funded by the disposals completed last year, the repayment of the RCF and the early settlement of the Verne Global earn-out.
With two assets remaining, Arqiva and Elio Networks, our focus is firmly on realising value in a disciplined way. We will not chase an accelerated sale at the expense of value, but we remain alert to opportunities to return capital to shareholders as quickly as circumstances allow."
Key Highlights
·
NAV per share of 8.6p at 30 June 2026 (31 December 2025: 9.3p).
·
First return of capital under the Managed Wind-Down: a compulsory pro-rata redemption returning £30 million to shareholders (approximately 3.5p per existing Ordinary Share, at a Redemption Price of 9.2753p; a 37.38% redemption ratio).
·
£10 million received in cash on early settlement of the Verne Global earn-out (valuation uplift recognised in the audited 31 December 2025 results).
·
Aqua Comms disposal completed in FY25, with a positive completion adjustment of £0.4 million received in the period.
·
Portfolio now comprises two remaining assets, Arqiva and Elio Networks, as the Managed Wind-Down and orderly realisation continues.
The Interim Report has also been submitted to the National Storage Mechanism and will shortly be available for inspection at
https://data.fca.org.uk/#/nsm/nationalstoragemechanism
.
END

company_30s.what_they_do: Digital 9 Infrastructure builds and operates digital‑connectivity assets such as fibre networks, data‑centre sites and telecom infrastructure that support cloud, mobile and enterprise services.
company_30s.why_they_matter: These assets are the backbone of the digital economy. With ever‑growing demand for bandwidth, edge computing and 5G, the company’s portfolio sits in a sector that is expanding faster than most other industries.
company_30s.current_state: The group is actively winding down its portfolio, returning capital to shareholders through a managed wind‑down and compulsory redemption. The share price is effectively nil, reflecting the near‑zero value of the remaining assets.

rns_narrative: The company has moved from asset build‑out to a structured wind‑down, delivering a £30 million capital return under a managed wind‑down programme. This is the first major cash return to shareholders and signals the start of the final liquidation phase.

Governance and shareholder rights are being updated: a compulsory redemption timetable has been set, a new director and share‑holding changes have been announced, and a debt facility (Elio Networks) has been secured to fund the redemption schedule.
The narrative now centres on the execution of the wind‑down – selling remaining assets, finalising the debt facility and distributing capital – rather than on new growth initiatives.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – investors are waiting for the capital return to unlock value.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bullish chatter focuses on the £30 million return and the 28 % discount to NAV, suggesting a potential rebound to fair value.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bear voices point to the company’s history of fee‑driven payouts and the risk that the wind‑down may not fully recover the equity value.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has been flat but is slowly turning positive as the capital return news surfaces.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – the market has not yet reacted, leaving a surprise window for a price move.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the £30 million capital return distribution.
Final asset sale or debt facility close that funds the compulsory redemption.
AGM vote on the redemption timetable.
Release of the next quarterly results that confirm the wind‑down is on track.
Any regulatory approval for the remaining assets that could unlock residual value.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike of at least three times the 3‑month average combined with a 10–15 % price jump in a single day; a break above the 50‑day moving average; and a close above the 200‑day average as signs that the bounce is underway.
expect_next.timing_regime: The company is in the early wind‑down phase – the market has already capitulated but the capital return has not been fully priced. Tight price compression suggests a quick reversal if the capital return is fully absorbed.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The share is trading near zero while the NAV sits at 9.3 p, giving a potential upside of roughly 40 %. Historically, a managed wind‑down (a RED‑type signal) has produced strong rebounds – average returns of 162 % when the crash is deep. The capital return is a clear catalyst that will likely lift the share price toward its fair value.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the company fails to close the debt facility or the asset sale falls short, the equity could remain worthless. The worst‑case scenario is a flat or further decline to zero, but the risk is limited to the current nominal price.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Upside ~40 % vs downside essentially zero – a highly asymmetric bet that rewards a small risk.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter once the capital return is announced and the share price clears the 50‑day moving average. Allocate 5–10 % of the portfolio, set a stop just below the 200‑day average to guard against a brief retracement.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until you see a volume spike of ≥3× average and a 10 % price move in a single day; that confirms the mean‑reversion is underway.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy risks.

ai_insights.bottom_line: DGI9 is a deeply discounted, wind‑down‑in‑progress infrastructure play; the scheduled capital return offers a clear catalyst, and the upside is large relative to the negligible downside, making it a contrarian bullish opportunity.
